Looking at the LZSS compression format from the documentation, I need to understand the encoding scheme: it uses a 4096-byte sliding window where matches are found by scanning from nearest to oldest positions, preferring longer matches or nearest matches of equal length. The format groups tokens into 8-token blocks preceded by a flag byte where each bit indicates whether that token is a literal (1) or a match reference (0), with literals taking 1 byte and matches taking 2 bytes to encode the position and length information.

static void hmac_seed(sdk_sha256_ctx *inner, sdk_sha256_ctx *outer,
const unsigned char k0[SDK_HMAC_SHA256_BLOCK_LEN]) {
unsigned char pad[SDK_HMAC_SHA256_BLOCK_LEN];
size_t i;
for (i = 0; i < SDK_HMAC_SHA256_BLOCK_LEN; ++i) {
pad[i] = (unsigned char)(k0[i] ^ 0x36u);
}
sdk_sha256_init(inner);
sdk_sha256_update(inner, pad, sizeof pad);
for (i = 0; i < SDK_HMAC_SHA256_BLOCK_LEN; ++i) {
pad[i] = (unsigned char)(k0[i] ^ 0x5cu);
}
sdk_sha256_init(outer);
sdk_sha256_update(outer, pad, sizeof pad);
sdk_secure_wipe(pad, sizeof pad);
}


This is correct. inner = H((k0^ipad) || ...), outer = H((k0^opad) || ...).

c


typedef enum sdk_tech {
SDK_TECH_NONE = 0,
SDK_TECH_NAKED_SINGLE = 1,
SDK_TECH_HIDDEN_SINGLE = 2,
SDK_TECH_LOCKED_POINTING = 3,
SDK_TECH_LOCKED_CLAIMING = 4,
SDK_TECH_NAKED_PAIR = 5,
SDK_TECH_HIDDEN_PAIR = 6,
SDK_TECH_NAKED_TRIPLE = 7,
SDK_TECH_HIDDEN_TRIPLE = 8
} sdk_tech;

typedef enum sdk_step_kind { SDK_STEP_PLACE = 0, SDK_STEP_ELIM = 1 } sdk_step_kind;

typedef struct sdk_logic_step {
sdk_tech tech;
sdk_step_kind kind;
int target_cell;       /* primary target (placement) or -1 */
int placed_digit;      /* for placement */
int candidate_mask_before; /* for target */
int candidate_mask_after;
int target_cells[81];  int target_count;     /* affected cells (eliminations) */
int affected_candidates; /* mask removed */
int support_cells[81]; int support_count;
int support_units[27]; int support_unit_count; /* unit indices 0..26 (row0..8,col0..8,box0..8) */
int score_weight;
/* textual params derived deterministically */
char conclusion[128];
char reason[256];
} sdk_logic_step;


The logic solver runs from the current board state. It computes candidates, then scans techniques in priority order. Each technique, when it finds a step, returns it. The "run" applies the step (for full solve) or returns it (for hint).


For difficulty scoring: run the full logic solver, accumulating the score (weight per effective step), max technique, count per technique. If it stalls (no step found but board not complete), mark stalled.


This is a substantial but well-defined algorithm. Let me implement it.


Generator (spec §13-§15, §27, §28):


Generate full valid grid: start from empty, fill via randomized backtracking (search solver with random order), or start from a known solution and permute. The spec says "不得只對一個固定解盤做有限少量位置交換" and allows permutations as extra randomization. I'll do randomized full-grid generation via backtracking with shuffled candidate order, seeded by BCryptGenRandom or a test seed.


Dig holes: remove clues in random order, check uniqueness (count_solutions limit=2), keep if still unique, until reaching target clue range for the difficulty.


Classify difficulty via logic solver on the puzzle.


Retry with guards.


Difficulty classification (spec §12):


Easy: only T1/T2, at least one T2, score 20-120, clues 36-49.


Medium: at least one T3-T6, no T7/T8, score 70-260, clues 30-40.


Hard: at least one T7/T8, or ≥3 T5/T6 and score≥220, score 180-520, clues 24-34.


The generator picks a difficulty, generates, classifies, and if it doesn't match the requested difficulty, retries (or adjusts). For fixed-seed determinism (spec §21, §29), the generator must be deterministic given (seed, difficulty).


Hint (spec §16-§17, §24):


Validate conflicts, confirm ≥1 solution, compute derived candidates, find first logic step, return structured hint (preview, don't modify board).


Placement hint apply: fill one target value, mark hint-assisted, peer-note removal per settings, single undo transaction.


Elimination hint apply: remove only existing notes matching step, no new notes.


Must not read stored solution. Implementation naturally doesn't (it uses only current formal values + logic solver).


Auto Solve (spec §18): conflict validation, if unsatisfiable report, else solve via search solver, mark auto-solved.

typedef struct {
uint8_t g[81];
long nodes;
long node_limit;
int limit;       /* for counting */
int count;       /* accumulated, capped at limit+1 */
int solved;      /* for solve_one */
int mode;        /* 0 = solve_one, 1 = count */
} sctx;


Recursion:


c


static void rec(sctx *c) {
int cell = -1, best = 10, i;
if (c->nodes++ > c->node_limit) return;  /* guard */
/* find min-candidate empty cell */
for (i = 0; i < 81; ++i) {
if (c->g[i] == 0) {
int cnt = candidate_count(c->g, i);
if (cnt == 0) return;  /* dead end */
if (cnt < best) { best = cnt; cell = i; if (best == 1) break; }
}
}
if (cell == -1) {
/* solved */
if (c->mode == 0) { c->solved = 1; }
else { c->count++; if (c->count > c->limit) c->count = c->limit + 1; }
return;
}
/* try digits 1..9 in order */
int d;
uint8_t saved = c->g[cell];
for (d = 1; d <= 9; ++d) {
if (is_candidate(c->g, cell, d)) {
c->g[cell] = (uint8_t)d;
rec(c);
c->g[cell] = saved;
if (c->mode == 0 && c->solved) return;
if (c->mode == 1 && c->count > c->limit) return;
}
}
}


candidate_count / is_candidate check row/col/box.

c


int sdk_logic_solve(const sdk_board *in, sdk_board *out, sdk_logic_trace *trace) {
sdk_board work; sdk_board_copy(in, &work);
sdk_cand masks[81];
derive (fresh) into masks;
init trace;
for (;;) {
/* recompute masks consistency: masks[c] = base & masks[c] for empty */
for each empty c: masks[c] = base_candidates(&work,c) & masks[c];
/* check stall: empty cell with masks==0 */
for each empty c: if masks[c]==0 -> stalled=1, goto done;
if no empty cells -> solved, goto done;
sdk_logic_step step;
if (!find_step(&work, masks, &step)) { stalled=1; goto done; }
/* apply */
apply_step(&work, masks, &step);
/* accumulate trace */
trace->logic_score += step.score_weight;
trace->step_count++;
if (step.tech > trace->max_technique) trace->max_technique = step.tech;
trace->tech_counts[step.tech]++;
}
done:
if (out) sdk_board_copy(&work, out);
return 1;
}

void sdk_classify_difficulty(const sdk_board *puzzle, sdk_difficulty_result *out) {
run logic_solve fully -> get trace (must solve, not stall).
if stalled -> difficulty=UNKNOWN, stalled=1.

Easy: max_tech <= HIDDEN_SINGLE (i.e., only T1/T2 used), tech_counts[T2]>=1 (at least one hidden single), logic_score in [20,120], clue in [36,49].

Hard: (at least one T7/T8) OR (tech_counts[T5]+tech_counts[T6]>=3 AND score>=220); score in [180,520]; clue in [24,34].

Now the generator. Let me think about generation:


Generate a full valid solution grid with randomized backtracking (seeded).

But to hit the clue range AND difficulty simultaneously is the hard part. Strategy:


Generate full solution.

Simpler robust approach:

Better:


Target clue count = pick a value in the requested difficulty's clue range (e.g., Easy ~40-45, Medium ~34-38, Hard ~28-32).

This "random subset of size target_clues, check unique + classify" is simpler and controllable. But a random subset of size N from a solution often yields multiple solutions (not unique) for small N, and uniqueness is more likely for larger N. For Easy (N~40) uniqueness is usually easy. For Hard (N~28-30) uniqueness requires care; random subset of 28 from a solution — there are many minimal-ish puzzles. It may need retries. With guards and retries it should work.


But the spec §14 requires the proper dig approach (remove one at a time, verify uniqueness, keep if unique) to guarantee uniqueness. Full grid generation via backtracking with shuffled digit order from the PRNG:


plaintext

Let me implement a PRNG in the gen file: splitmix64.


c


static uint64_t g_rng_state;
static uint64_t next_rand(void) { g_rng_state += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL; uint64_t z = g_rng_state; z = (z ^ (z>>30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9ULL; z = (z ^ (z>>27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EBULL; return z ^ (z>>31); }
static void seed_rng(uint64_t s){ g_rng_state = s ? s : 0x123456789ULL; }
static void shuffle(int *arr, int n) { for i=n-1..1: j = next_rand() % (i+1); swap; }

static uint64_t rng_state;
static uint64_t sm_next(void){
rng_state += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL;
uint64_t z = rng_state;
z = (z ^ (z>>30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9ULL;
z = (z ^ (z>>27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EBULL;
return z ^ (z>>31);
}
static void sm_seed(uint64_t s){ rng_state = s ? s : 0x123456789ABCDEF0ULL; }
static void sm_shuffle_int(int *a, int n){
int i;
for (i = n-1; i > 0; --i){
uint64_t r = sm_next();
int j = (int)(r % (uint64_t)(i+1));
int t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t;
}
}

sdk_generate:


plaintext


void sdk_generate(params, out, solution, seed_out, report){
memset report.
uint64_t seed = params->fixed_seed ? params->seed : random_seed_from_os();
report->seed_used = seed;
start = wallclock.
int target = target_for(params->requested);  // base target
int accepted = 0;
int regen = 0;
for (regen = 0; regen < MAX_REGEN; regen++){
uint64_t s = seed + (uint64_t)regen * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL;
sm_seed(s);
sdk_board full;
if (!generate_full_grid(&full)) continue;
if (solution) sdk_board_copy(&full, solution);
int attempts = 0;
for (attempts = 0; attempts < params->candidate_attempts; attempts++){
if (wall_guard_exceeded(start, params->wall_guard_ms)) break;
report->attempts++;
int t = target + (sm_next() % 7) - 3;  // vary target within +/-3
clamp t to requested clue range.
sdk_board puzzle = full (copy);
dig(&puzzle, t);
sdk_difficulty_result dr;
sdk_classify_difficulty(&puzzle, &dr);
if (!dr.stalled && dr.difficulty == params->requested){
sdk_board_copy(&puzzle, out);
accepted = 1;
report->accepted = 1;
report->actual = dr.difficulty;
report->clue_count = dr.clue_count;
report->logic_score = dr.logic_score;
report->max_technique = dr.max_technique;
{ int ti; for (ti=1;ti<=8;ti++) report->tech_counts[ti] = dr.tech_counts[ti]; }
report->regenerations = regen;
report->duration_ms = elapsed(start);
return;  // success
}
}
if (wall_guard_exceeded(...)) break;
}
report->accepted = 0;
report->reject_reason = "exhausted generations/attempts or wall guard";
report->duration_ms = elapsed(start);
}

PRNG: xoshiro256**


plaintext


static uint64_t rotl(uint64_t x, int k){ return (x << k) | (x >> (64-k)); }
static uint64_t xr_next(uint64_t s[4]) {
uint64_t res = rotl(s[1]*5,7)*9;
uint64_t t = s[1] << 17;
s[2] ^= s[0]; s[3] ^= s[1];
s[1] ^= s[2]; s[0] ^= s[3];
s[2] ^= t;
s[3] = rotl(s[3],45);
return res;
}


Seed xoshiro: splitmix64 to expand a 64-bit seed into 4 states:


plaintext


static uint64_t splitmix64(uint64_t *x){ uint64_t z=(*x+=0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL); z=(z^(z>>30))*0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9ULL; z=(z^(z>>27))*0x94D049BB133111EBULL; return z^(z>>31); }


For full grid generation with diagonal fill + randomized solve:


plaintext


static void shuffle_int(int *arr, int n, uint64_t s[4]) {
for (int i=n-1;i>0;i--){ int j = xr_next(s) % (i+1); int t=arr[i]; arr[i]=arr[j]; arr[j]=t; }
}

static void fill_diagonal(sdk_board *b, uint64_t s[4]) {
int box;
for (box=0; box<9; box+=3) {  // boxes 0,4,8
int nums[9]; for(int i=0;i<9;i++) nums[i]=i+1;
shuffle_int(nums,9,s);
for(int i=0;i<9;i++){ int r=box/3*3 + i/3 + (box%3); ... }
}
}

For each diagonal box, fill its 9 cells with nums[0..8] in row-major order within the box.

static int r_solve(sdk_board *b, uint64_t s[4], long *nodes, long limit) {
if (*nodes > limit) return 0; (*nodes)++;
// find MRV cell
int cell=-1,best=10;
for(...) if empty: n=cand_count; if n==0 return 0; if n<best { best=n; cell=i;}
if(cell==-1) return 1; // solved
// try digits 1..9 in shuffled order
int order[9]; for i order[i]=i+1; shuffle(order,9,s);
for k: d=order[k]; if cell_ok(b,cell,d){ b->cells[cell].value=d; if(r_solve(...)) return 1; b->cells[cell].value=0; }
return 0;
}

static int grid_ok(const sdk_board *b, int cell, int d) {
int r = cell / 9, c = cell % 9, br = (r / 3) * 3, bc = (c / 3) * 3, i;
for (i = 0; i < 9; ++i) {
if (b->cells[r * 9 + i].value == (uint8_t)d) return 0;   // row
if (b->cells[i * 9 + c].value == (uint8_t)d) return 0;   // column
}
for (i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
int j;
for (j = 0; j < 3; ++j)
if (b->cells[(br + i) * 9 + (bc + j)].value == (uint8_t)d) return 0;  // box
}
return 1;
}

plaintext


int sdk_generate_once(uint64_t seed, sdk_difficulty req, const sdk_gen_params *p, sdk_board *out, sdk_board *solution, sdk_difficulty_result *dr) {
uint64_t s[4];
sdk_board full;
int lo, hi;
(void)p;
if (req==EASY){lo=36;hi=49;} else if (req==MEDIUM){lo=30;hi=40;} else if (req==HARD){lo=24;hi=34;} else {lo=24;hi=49; return 0;}
xr_seed(s, seed);
generate_full_grid(s, &full);
{
int o;
for (o = 0; o < 24; ++o) {
int order[81], i;
for (i=0;i<81;i++) order[i]=i;
shuffle_int(order, 81, s);
{
sdk_board puzzle;
sdk_board_copy(&full, &puzzle);
for (i=0;i<81;i++){
int cell=order[i];
uint8_t saved; int stalled, unique, cnt;
if (puzzle.cells[cell].value==0) continue;
saved=puzzle.cells[cell].value;
puzzle.cells[cell].value=0; puzzle.cells[cell].origin=EMPTY;
unique=puzzle_is_unique(&puzzle,&stalled);
if(!unique){ puzzle.cells[cell].value=saved; puzzle.cells[cell].origin=GIVEN; continue; }
cnt=count_given(&puzzle);
if (cnt<lo) break;
if (cnt<=hi && !stalled){
sdk_difficulty_result local;
sdk_classify_difficulty(&puzzle,&local);
if (local.difficulty==req){
if(dr) memcpy(dr,&local,sizeof local);
finalize_puzzle(&puzzle,out,solution);
return 1;
}
}
}
}
}
}
return 0;
}

Pointing (T3):

For each box u (18..26), for each digit d:

Claiming (T4):

if all L in same box b: targets = empty cells in box b NOT in the unit, having d candidate. If any → step.


Naked Pair (T5):

For each unit, find two distinct empty cells with identical candidate mask of popcount exactly 2. Eliminate those two digits from all OTHER empty cells in the unit that contain them. (targets = cells in unit, not the pair, empty, with (mask & pairmask) != 0). If any → step.


Hidden Pair (T6):

For each unit, for each unordered pair of digits (d1,d2): collect empty cells in unit whose candidates include d1 or d2. If exactly 2 such cells, and their combined mask has bits beyond {d1,d2} (i.e., other candidates to remove), eliminate those other candidates from those 2 cells. If any removal → step.


Naked Triple (T7):

For each unit, for each triple of distinct empty cells where each has popcount 2 or 3, union of the three masks has popcount exactly 3, and each cell's mask is a subset of the union: eliminate union from other empty cells in unit that contain any union digit. If any → step.


Hidden Triple (T8):

For each unit, for each triple of digits (d1,d2,d3): collect empty cells whose candidates include any of d1,d2,d3. If exactly 3 such cells, and they have other candidates beyond {d1,d2,d3}, eliminate those other candidates. If any → step.

plaintext


static int box_index_of(int cell) {
int r = cell / 9, c = cell % 9;
return (r / 3) * 3 + (c / 3);
}

static int scan_pointing(const sdk_board *b, sdk_cand *m, sdk_logic_step *s) {
int d, u;
for (d = 1; d <= 9; ++d) {
for (u = 18; u < 27; ++u) {
int cells[9], i, lst[9], ln = 0;
int brow = (u - 18) / 3, bcol = (u - 18) % 3;
unit_cells(u, cells);
for (i = 0; i < 9; ++i) {
int cc = cells[i];
if (is_empty(b, cc) && (m[cc] & SDK_CAND_BIT(d))) lst[ln++] = cc;
}
if (ln == 0) continue;
/* same row? */
{
int rr = lst[0] / 9, same = 1, i2;
for (i2 = 0; i2 < ln; ++i2) if (lst[i2] / 9 != rr) { same = 0; break; }
if (same) {
int targets[9], tn = 0, cc2;
for (cc2 = rr * 9; cc2 < rr * 9 + 9; ++cc2) {
if ((cc2 % 9) / 3 != bcol && is_empty(b, cc2) &&
(m[cc2] & SDK_CAND_BIT(d))) targets[tn++] = cc2;
}
if (tn > 0) {
... build step (ELIM, affected=d, targets, support=lst, units=u and row rr) ...
return 1;
}
}
}
/* same col? */
{
int cc0 = lst[0] % 9, same = 1, i2;
for (i2 = 0; i2 < ln; ++i2) if (lst[i2] % 9 != cc0) { same = 0; break; }
if (same) {
int targets[9], tn = 0, rr2;
for (rr2 = 0; rr2 < 9; ++rr2) {
int cc2 = rr2 * 9 + cc0;
if ((cc2 / 9) / 3 != brow && is_empty(b, cc2) &&
(m[cc2] & SDK_CAND_BIT(d))) targets[tn++] = cc2;
}
if (tn > 0) { ... return 1; }
}
}
}
}
return 0;
}


This is correct. The key fix: use box-column comparison (cc2 % 9) / 3 != bcol for row pointing, and box-row (cc2/9)/3 != brow for column pointing.

The real issue is INSIDE sdk_logic_solve's mask management. I should just FIX it. The bug is clear in principle: m[i] &= base_candidates(&work, i) in the solve loop and local[i] &= base_candidates in find_step RESTORE eliminated candidates.


Actually, wait. Let me re-examine. The purpose of m[i] &= base_candidates is to keep masks consistent with current board values (a cell's candidates can only shrink as peers get filled). It's meant to DROP candidates that became impossible due to NEW placements. It should NOT restore candidates that were deliberately eliminated by logic.


The problem: base_candidates returns ALL valid candidates, not just the ones not-yet-eliminated. So ANDing with base_candidates restores eliminated ones.


The CORRECT design: maintain a fixed set of candidates (the logic-deduced "this cell cannot be d" facts) separately from the base candidates. An elimination adds to the "excluded" set. The effective candidate = base_candidates & ~excluded. The m[i] &= base_candidates should only ever REMOVE candidates (when a peer is placed, base_candidates shrinks), never ADD. But m[i] &= base_candidates where base_candidates is a SUPERSET of m[i] (since m[i] should be subset of base_candidates) does nothing harmful IF m[i] is always a subset. But if m[i] had d removed (eliminated), and base_candidates includes d, then m[i] & base_candidates = m[i] WITH d restored (since d was in base_candidates). That ADDS d back. Bug.


The fix: the line should be m[i] = m[i] & base_candidates — but that's what it is, and it ADDS back because base_candidates is a superset. To prevent adding back, we should only remove, not restore. But we can't just remove-from-base because base_candidates is the source of truth for "not yet eliminated".


The cleanest fix: maintain eliminations in a SEPARATE mask excluded[81]. Effective candidates = base_candidates & ~excluded. When an elimination step removes digit d from cell c, do excluded[c] |= d (accumulate). Then m[i] = base_candidates(i) & ~excluded[i]. This way eliminations persist across iterations, and new placements correctly shrink base_candidates (reducing m further).


This requires restructuring sdk_logic_solve and sdk_logic_find_step to carry an excluded mask. But the public API sdk_logic_find_step(b, masks, out) takes masks as the candidate masks. The semantics: masks are the CURRENT candidate sets (already excluding eliminated digits). The issue is the & base_candidates restore.


Actually, the SIMPLEST fix that preserves the API: change the consistency line from m[i] &= base_candidates(&work, i) to NOT restore eliminated candidates. But base_candidates is the only source. Hmm.


Alternative simpler fix: In sdk_logic_solve, instead of re-deriving via m[i] &= base_candidates, track eliminations separately. Let me restructure:


c


int sdk_logic_solve(const sdk_board *in, sdk_board *out, sdk_logic_trace *trace) {
sdk_board work;
sdk_cand m[81];        /* current candidate masks (effective) */
memset(trace, 0, sizeof *trace);
sdk_board_copy(in, &work);
if (!sdk_derive_candidates(&work, m)) { trace->stalled = 1; ... return 1; }

for (;;) {
int empty = 0;
for (i = 0; i < 81; ++i) {
if (is_empty(&work, i)) {
empty++;
sdk_cand base = base_candidates(&work, i);  /* from values */
/* keep existing eliminations: m[i] must stay subset of base,
* but must NOT regain digits already eliminated. */
m[i] &= base;   /* this DROPS newly-impossible, but also... */
...
}
}
...
}
}


The fundamental problem: base_candidates regenerates the full candidate set, so it can't "remember" eliminations.


THE FIX: Don't recompute from scratch each iteration. Instead:


Initialize m[i] = base_candidates at start.


On each placement (a digit d placed in cell c), update m: for c and its peers, m drops d (because d is now placed). Actually for the placed cell, m[c] = EMPTY. For peers, m[peer] &= ~d.


On each elimination, m[target] &= ~affected.


This way m only ever SHRINKS (monotonic), and eliminations persist naturally. base_candidates is only used for the INITIAL derivation.


This is the correct, standard approach. The current code's bug is calling m[i] &= base_candidates(&work, i) which RE-EXPANDS m[i] to the full base set, wiping eliminations.


So the fix:


Remove the m[i] &= base_candidates(&work, i) line in the solve loop. Instead, update m incrementally: after a placement, for the placed cell and peers, remove the digit. After an elimination, remove affected digits from targets.


But we still need to ensure m[i] never includes a digit that's been placed in a peer. Since we update m on each placement to drop d from peers, m stays consistent.


For find_step with in_masks: it does local[i] &= base_candidates(b,i). This also re-expands. But if the caller passes masks that already have eliminations, the & base_candidates would wipe them. So in sdk_logic_solve, we should pass m WITHOUT the base_candidates restoration, OR find_step should not restore.

static sdk_cand base_candidates(const sdk_board *b, int cell) {
int r = cell / 9, c = cell % 9, br = (r / 3) * 3, bc = (c / 3) * 3, i;
sdk_cand m = SDK_CAND_ALL;
for (i = 0; i < 9; ++i) {
int v;
v = b->cells[r * 9 + i].value; if (v >= 1 && v <= 9) m &= ~SDK_CAND_BIT(v);
v = b->cells[i * 9 + c].value; if (v >= 1 && v <= 9) m &= ~SDK_CAND_BIT(v);

int j;

if (v >= 1 && v <= 9) m &= ~SDK_CAND_BIT(v);
}
}
return m;
}

Let me re-examine apply_to_masks:


c


static void apply_to_masks(sdk_cand *m, const sdk_board *work, const sdk_logic_step *step) {
int i;
(void)work;
if (step->kind == SDK_STEP_PLACE) {
int c = step->target_cell, d = step.placed_digit;
int peers[20], pn = sdk_peers(c, peers);
m[c] = SDK_CAND_EMPTY;
for (i = 0; i < pn; ++i) m[peers[i]] &= ~SDK_CAND_BIT(d);
} else {
for (i = 0; i < step->target_count; ++i)
m[step->target_cells[i]] &= ~step->affected_candidates;
}
}


This correctly removes digits from masks. For placement: m[c]=EMPTY, peers lose d. For elimination: targets lose affected_candidates. Correct.


And the solve loop's m[i] &= base_candidates only removes (preserves eliminations). So eliminations persist. So after a pointing elimination removes d from cell X, X keeps d gone. So subsequent find_step sees X without d. So a naked single can be enabled.

Suppose cell X has candidates {1,2,3,4}. A pointing elimination removes digit 1 (affected=bit1). apply_to_masks: m[X] &= ~bit1 → m[X] = {2,3,4}.

Solve loop:


m[i] &= base_candidates(&work, i) for empty cells. This can only REMOVE bits from m[i]. So if an elimination removed bit d from m[c] in the previous iteration, m[c] lacks d. m[c] &= base_candidates(c) — base_candidates(c) includes d (not placed), so m[c] stays (d still gone). PERSISTS. Good.


find_step(&work, m, &step): copies m to local, then local[i] &= base_candidates(b,i). Same — preserves eliminations. Scans T1-T8 on local (= m with eliminations).


So eliminations ARE visible to find_step. So if a pointing elimination removed d from cell X, the next find_step sees X without d. So a naked single at X (if X had only d left after elimination) would be found. So eliminations enable progress.

Flow:

sdk_vault_save(vault, store): generate fresh nonce, encrypt, atomic replace with backup (ReplaceFileW).

static int clone_tx_arr(sdk_undo_transaction **dst, uint32_t *dstn, const sdk_undo_transaction *src, uint32_t n) {
*dstn = n; *dst = NULL;
if (n == 0) return 1;
*dst = calloc(n, sizeof(sdk_undo_transaction));
if (!*dst) return 0;
for (uint32_t i=0;i<n;i++){
(*dst)[i].action_kind = src[i].action_kind;
(*dst)[i].assisted_reason = src[i].assisted_reason;
(*dst)[i].change_count = src[i].change_count;
(*dst)[i].sequence_number = src[i].sequence_number;
if (src[i].change_count){
(*dst)[i].changes = calloc(src[i].change_count, sizeof(sdk_change));
if (!(*dst)[i].changes) return 0;
memcpy((*dst)[i].changes, src[i].changes, src[i].change_count*sizeof(sdk_change));
} else (*dst)[i].changes = NULL;
}
return 1;
}
static sdk_status sdk_store_add_game(sdk_store *s, const sdk_game_record *g) {
... realloc games ...
sdk_game_record *dst = &s->games[s->game_count];
memcpy(dst, g, sizeof *g);  /* shallow copy pointers first */

if (!clone_tx_arr(&dst->redo, &dst->redo_count, g->redo, g->redo_count)) { free undo; return NOMEM; }
s->game_count++;
return SDK_OK;
}

So write does: undo_count, undo[], redo_count, redo[]

read does: undo_count, redo_count, undo[], redo[]


THE ORDER MISMATCHES! The writer writes undo_count, then undo txs, then redo_count, then redo txs. But the reader reads undo_count, then redo_count, then undo txs, then redo txs.


So when reading: after reading undo_count=uc, it reads redo_count=rc (but the bytes there are actually the first undo tx!). This corrupts everything. That's the bug!


This is a classic serialization order bug. The write order and read order for undo_count/redo_count vs undo/redo arrays don't match.

void sdk_draw_modal_backdrop(sdk_ui *ui, sdk_rect panel,

I'll keep it clean:


c


typedef struct { sdk_rect grid; int cell; } play_layout;
static play_layout _play_layout(int w, int h) {
int pad = 18;
int topbar = 64;
int bottom = 200;     /* numpad + actions */
int avail = h - topbar - bottom - pad*2;
int gs = (w - pad*2);
if (gs > avail) gs = avail;
if (gs > 720) gs = 720;
int gx = (w - gs)/2;
int gy = topbar + ((avail - gs)/2);
play_layout L; L.grid.x=gx; L.grid.y=gy; L.grid.w=gs; L.grid.h=gs; L.cell=gs/9;
return L;
}


Cell from point: if inside grid, col = (x-gx)/cell, row=(y-gy)/cell, idx=row*9+col.


Number pad: 9 buttons in a row at bottom. Each button width = (w - pad*2)/9 - gap. Place at y = h - 150. Plus a second row of action buttons: Undo, Redo, Notes(toggle), Erase, Hint, Auto, Menu.

Let me write entry:


c


#include "app/sdk_app.h"
#include "platform/sdk_platform.h"
#include <windows.h>
#include <wchar.h>

int WINAPI WinMain(HINSTANCE hInst, HINSTANCE hPrev, LPSTR cmdline, int nshow) {
(void)hInst;(void)hPrev;(void)cmdline;(void)nshow;
const wchar_t *vault = NULL, *pw = NULL;
int prod = 1;
for (int i = 1; i < __argc; ++i) {
if (wcscmp(__wargv[i], L"--vault")==0 && i+1<__argc) vault = __wargv[++i];
else if (wcscmp(__wargv[i], L"--pw")==0 && i+1<__argc) pw = __wargv[++i];
else if (wcscmp(__wargv[i], L"--test-iters")==0) prod = 0;
}
sdk_app *app = sdk_app_create(960, 720, vault, pw, prod);
if (!app) return 1;
int rc = sdk_platform_run(app, L"Sudoku");
sdk_app_destroy(app);
return rc;
}


__argc/__wargv require <stdlib.h> and are MSVC-specific; they're available when linking the CRT (we link /MT, so CRT is static). Good. Include <stdlib.h>.

bat


@echo off
setlocal EnableDelayedExpansion

CLI: locstat [--config PATH] [--json PATH] [--category NAME] [--fail-on-error] [--no-default-excludes] ROOT. Exactly one ROOT. Unknown option / missing value / unknown --category => usage error (exit 2). --json - => JSON to stdout, human summary to stderr. --help => exit 0.

Canonical formats you MUST implement exactly (from docs/19):


§6 Repository layout:

.tinyvcs/

FORMAT        (content exactly ASCII "tinyvcs 1\n")

HEAD          (content "ref: refs/heads/<branch>\n")

index

objects/aa/<rest>   (first 2 hex of 64-hex object ID as dir)

refs/heads/<branch>

locks/

tmp/


No detached HEAD. Metadata files must not be reparse points.


§8 Object identity: canonical unhashed bytes = <type> SP <len-decimal> NUL <payload> where type∈{blob,tree,commit}. Object ID = SHA-256 of those bytes, shown as 64 lowercase hex. The on-disk envelope stores only the payload (not the prefix); to verify the ID, rebuild canonical bytes from envelope type + decompressed payload. CRC32 also over payload bytes.


§9 Blob payload = exact file bytes (no newline translation).

§10 Tree payload: entries serialized in order:

u8 entry_type (1=file,2=dir)

u8 file_flags (bit0=FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY; dir must be 0; other bits 0)

u16 name_length

name bytes (single component, no '/' or NUL, length 1..255)

32-byte raw object id

Entry count not stored; parse to end. Entries MUST be sorted by Windows ordinal ignore-case strictly ascending; case-collision/duplicate/out-of-order tree => malformed.


§11 Commit payload:

u8 format_version (1)

u8 parent_count (0 or 1)

[parent 32 bytes] (if parent_count==1)

root_tree 32 bytes

i64 timestamp_epoch_ms

u16 author_length

author bytes (printable ASCII 32..126, 1..128 bytes, no leading/trailing space)

u32 message_length

message bytes (UTF-8, 1..4096 bytes, not all whitespace, may contain newline, no NUL)

At most one parent in v1.0.


§12 On-disk object envelope (.tinyvcs/objects/aa/...):

8 bytes magic "TVCSOBJ1"

u8 storage_mode (0=raw,1=lzss)

u8 object_type (1=blob,2=tree,3=commit)

u16 reserved (must be 0)

u64 uncompressed_length

u64 stored_length

u32 crc32_uncompressed

32 bytes object_id

stored payload bytes

All header fields LE except magic. File total length MUST equal header + stored_length. Decompressed length MUST equal uncompressed_length. CRC, object ID, and canonical type must ALL verify. Use mode 1 only when LZSS strictly smaller than raw; otherwise raw (header flags mode).


§13 LZSS token format: use sdk_lzss_compress/decompress (already canonical).


§14 Index (.tinyvcs/index):

8 bytes magic "TVCSIDX1"

u32 entry_count

entries...

u32 crc32_of_all_previous_bytes

Entry:

u16 path_length

path bytes (canonical UTF-8, '/' separated, complete relative path)

u8 file_flags

u8 stage_state (0=present,1=deleted)

32-byte blob id (all 0 when deleted)

u64 file_size_snapshot

i64 mtime_100ns_snapshot

Entries sorted by full path Windows ordinal ignore-case; case-collision forbidden. Index is the staged snapshot; size/mtime are quick dirty checks, final dirty decision still by content hash.


§15 CLI contract:


Discovery: walk up from CWD to filesystem root looking for .tinyvcs/.


status sections in order: "On branch", "Staged changes", "Unstaged changes", "Untracked files", summary. Paths sorted ignore-case.


add: at least one path or --all; directory recurses; ignore-hit paths not added (warn if explicitly named); path missing => only --all or already-tracked can stage deletion, else usage/data error; either fully update index or not at all.


commit: -m exactly one message; author from TINYVCS_AUTHOR env (fail if missing/invalid); timestamp wall clock (allow fixed test time); write all objects + FlushFileBuffers, THEN atomic-update ref via ReplaceFileW/MoveFileExW; ref lock via CreateFileW CREATE_NEW share=0 (existing valid lock => busy). Empty staging must NOT create a commit. Non-empty message required. No half-written reference on failure.


branch: no name => list branches ASCII ascending, current prefixed "* "; name => create from HEAD (reject unborn HEAD), reject existing name. Names allow ASCII letters/digits/-/_//; forbid empty, ., .., leading/trailing /, consecutive //.


switch: only existing branch; preflight computes all added/modified/deleted paths; reject if it would overwrite a dirty tracked file or collide with untracked; apply via same-dir temporary sibling files + Win32 atomic move/replace (sdk_file_write_atomic_w); case-only rename uses temp intermediate; on any I/O failure during apply: HEAD/ref unchanged, index unchanged, revert already-changed paths from temp backup; only after full working-tree success update HEAD.


restore: default source=index; --source COMMIT from commit tree; path not in source => if currently tracked delete it, else reject; does not change index/HEAD/branch.


reset --hard COMMIT --yes: --yes required; preflight untracked collision; on success branch ref + index + working tree all point to COMMIT; do not delete non-conflicting untracked files.


verify: check FORMAT, HEAD, refs, index framing/CRC, all refs' reachable commit graph, commit/tree/blob envelope+CRC+SHA-256, referenced object existence/type, tree ordering/path rules; unreachable objects => warning only (don't fail verify); .tmp and stale locks => warning. Summary must include scanned/reachable/unreachable/corrupt/missing/malformed counts. Return non-zero if repository incomplete.


ignore: file ".tinyignore"; support empty lines, # comments, relative paths, *, **, trailing / dir rules, rule order. No ! negation. .tinyvcs/ always ignored, cannot be un-ignored.


Exit codes (docs/19 §3): 0 ok, 2 usage/path validation, 3 malformed repository/config, 4 I/O/permission/resource/system, 5 integrity verify problem, 70 unexpected internal invariant. Errors to stderr (stable English stage name + Win32 error code where relevant, docs/19 §29); never mix debug logs into stdout JSON. Never return 0 on failure.


Deliverables (write under D:\0820-sudoku-workbuddy\dev_tools\tinyvcs):


tinyvcs.c — CLI dispatch/arg parsing + command implementations (init/status/add/commit/log/branch/switch/restore/reset/show/verify/help). You may split into more .c files if helpful (e.g., tv_store.c, tv_walk.c) but keep it cohesive.


tinyvcs_core.h / tinyvcs_core.c — object store: write/read blob/tree/commit with envelope+LZSS+CRC32+SHA256, tree building from working dir or from another tree, commit creation, index load/save, ref/HEAD read/write with locking + atomic replace, ignore loading, diff (staged vs unstaged vs untracked), checkout apply with rollback.


test_tinyvcs.c — unit + scenario tests using dev_tools/test_harness/sdk_test.c. MUST cover (docs/04 §14): init + repeat init rejection; add/commit/status; staged vs unstaged diff; file add/modify/delete; identical-blob dedup; branch create + switch; dirty working tree blocks switch; untracked collision blocks switch; restore single file; reset to old commit; ignore pattern; SHA-256 known test vectors (e.g., SHA-256("abc") = ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad); CRC32 known vectors (CRC32("123456789") = 0xCBF43926); LZSS round-trip + empty + random + repeated data; object bit-flip corruption; missing object; interrupted reference update fixture. #include "app/sdk_app.h"
#include "ui/sdk_ui.h"
#include "sudoku/sdk_sudoku.h"
#include "common/sdk_common.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* replicate play layout to compute click coordinates (mirror of sdk_pages.c _play_layout) */
typedef struct { int x,y,w,h; } R;
static R menu_new_rect(int w){ return (R){ (w-320)/2, 330, 320, 56 }; }
static R menu_theme_rect(int w){ return (R){ (w-320)/2, 400, 155, 44 }; }
static R menu_tab_rect(int w,int idx){ int tw=360,th=44,x=(w-tw)/2,y=250,cw=tw/3; return (R){x+idx*cw,y,cw,th}; }

static void play_layout(int w,int h,int *gx,int *gy,int *gs,int *cell){
int pad=18,topbar=70,numpad_h=150,actions_h=56;
int bottom=numpad_h+actions_h+pad*2;
int avail=h-topbar-bottom-pad;
int g=w-pad*2; if(g>avail)g=avail; if(g>740)g=740; if(g<200)g=200;
*gx=(w-g)/2; *gy=topbar+((avail-g)/2>0?(avail-g)/2:0); *gs=g; *cell=g/9;
}
static int cell_center_x(int gx,int cell,int c){ return gx + (c%9)*cell + cell/2; }
static int cell_center_y(int gy,int cell,int r){ return gy + (r)*cell + cell/2; }

/* visrender.c - headless G9 visual-evidence harness (docs/06, docs/10 §9-10, docs/19 §24-25).
* Drives the REAL sdk_app through its public input API (same code path as the
* Win32 platform layer) and writes BMP screenshots + an animation frame
* sequence + a golden-scene manifest. No native controls, no display. */
#include "app/sdk_app.h"
#include "ui/sdk_ui.h"
#include "sudoku/sdk_sudoku.h"
#include "common/sdk_common.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

#define W 1280
#define H 800

/* ---- layout mirror (sdk_pages.c) so we can hit-test like a real pointer ---- */
typedef struct { int x,y,w,h; } R;
static R rmenu_new(int w){ return (R){ (w-320)/2, 330, 320, 56 }; }
static R rmenu_theme(int w){ return (R){ (w-320)/2, 400, 155, 44 }; }
static R rmenu_tab(int w,int idx){ int tw=360,x=(w-tw)/2,y=250,cw=tw/3; return (R){x+idx*cw,y,cw,44}; }
static void play_lay(int w,int h,int* gx,int* gy,int* gs,int* cell){
int pad=18,topbar=70,nh=150,ah=56,bottom=nh+ah+pad*2;
int avail=h-topbar-bottom-pad; int g=w-pad*2;
if(g>avail)g=avail; if(g>740)g=740; if(g<200)g=200;
*gx=(w-g)/2; *gy=topbar+((avail-g)/2>0?(avail-g)/2:0); *gs=g; *cell=g/9;
}
static void click_cell(sdk_app*a,int gx,int gy,int cell,int idx){
int c=idx%9,r=idx/9; int x=gx+c*cell+cell/2, y=gy+r*cell+cell/2;
sdk_app_on_mouse_down(a,x,y); sdk_app_on_mouse_up(a,x,y);
}
static void click_btn(sdk_app*a, R r){ sdk_app_on_mouse_down(a,r.x+r.w/2,r.y+r.h/2); sdk_app_on_mouse_up(a,r.x+r.w/2,r.y+r.h/2); }

static int save(sdk_app*a, sdk_fb*fb, const char*path){
sdk_app_render(a, fb);
return sdk_write_bmp(fb, path);
}


Then main: create app, fb.


For each scene, render then save. Use a manifest buffer (sdk_buf) to build JSON.

c


#include "test/sdk_test.h"
#include "sudoku/sdk_sudoku.h"
#include "common/sdk_common.h"
#include "common/sdk_crc32.h"
#include "crypto/sdk_crypto.h"   // sdk_xchacha20poly1305_encrypt/decrypt
#include "common/sdk_lzss.h"
#include "ui/sdk_ui.h"           // sdk_fb_create/destroy maybe
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

static void tc_gen_batch(sdk_test_ctx *t) {
sdk_difficulty reqs[3] = { EASY, MEDIUM, HARD };
const char *names[3] = {"EASY","MEDIUM","HARD"};
for (int di=0; di<3; di++) {
int got=0;
for (int i=0; i<200 && got<50; i++) {
sdk_gen_params p; sdk_gen_params_default(&p, reqs[di]);
p.fixed_seed = 1; p.seed = (uint64_t)(7000 + di*100000 + i);
sdk_board puzzle, sol; sdk_gen_report rep;
sdk_generate(&p, &puzzle, &sol, NULL, &rep);
SDK_T_TRUE(t, rep.accepted);
// unique
int cnt=0; SDK_T_TRUE(t, sdk_count_solutions(&puzzle,2,&cnt) && cnt==1);
// logic solvable + classify
sdk_board out; sdk_logic_trace tr;
SDK_T_TRUE(t, sdk_logic_solve(&puzzle,&out,&tr));
SDK_T_TRUE(t, tr.solved);
sdk_difficulty_result dr; sdk_classify_difficulty(&puzzle,&dr);
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, (int)dr.difficulty, (int)reqs[di]);
// band
if (reqs[di]==EASY){ SDK_T_TRUE(t, rep.clue_count>=36 && rep.clue_count<=49); SDK_T_TRUE(t, rep.logic_score>=20 && rep.logic_score<=120); SDK_T_TRUE(t, dr.max_technique<=SDK_TECH_HIDDEN_SINGLE); }
else if (reqs[di]==MEDIUM){ SDK_T_TRUE(t, rep.clue_count>=30 && rep.clue_count<=40); SDK_T_TRUE(t, rep.logic_score>=70 && rep.logic_score<=260); SDK_T_TRUE(t, dr.tech_counts[SDK_TECH_NAKED_TRIPLE]==0 && dr.tech_counts[SDK_TECH_HIDDEN_TRIPLE]==0); }
else { SDK_T_TRUE(t, rep.clue_count>=24 && rep.clue_count<=34); SDK_T_TRUE(t, rep.logic_score>=180 && rep.logic_score<=520); int t7t8=dr.tech_counts[SDK_TECH_NAKED_TRIPLE]+dr.tech_counts[SDK_TECH_HIDDEN_TRIPLE]; int t5t6=dr.tech_counts[SDK_TECH_NAKED_PAIR]+dr.tech_counts[SDK_TECH_HIDDEN_PAIR]; SDK_T_TRUE(t, t7t8>0 || (t5t6>=3 && rep.logic_score>=220)); }
got++;
}
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, got, 50);
sdk_test_evidence(t, "build/evidence/batch_ok.txt");  // maybe not
}
}

static void tc_crypto_roundtrip(sdk_test_ctx *t) {
for (int i=0;i<100;i++){
size_t n = 16 + (i*37)%200;
uint8_t *pt = malloc(n); uint8_t *ct=...; uint8_t *nonce=...; uint8_t key[32];
sdk_random_bytes(pt,n); sdk_random_bytes(key,32); sdk_random_bytes(nonce,24);
size_t ctcap = n + 64; ct=malloc(ctcap);
size_t ctlen; SDK_T_EQ_ST(t, sdk_xchacha20poly1305_encrypt(key,nonce,pt,n,NULL,0,ct,&ctlen), SDK_OK);
uint8_t *out=malloc(n+16);
size_t outlen; SDK_T_EQ_ST(t, sdk_xchacha20poly1305_decrypt(key,nonce,ct,ctlen,NULL,0,out,&outlen), SDK_OK);
SDK_T_EQ_MEM(t, pt, out, n);
// tamper -> fail
ct[0]^=1; SDK_T_EQ_ST(t, sdk_xchacha20poly1305_decrypt(key,nonce,ct,ctlen,NULL,0,out,&outlen), SDK_ERR_VERIFY);
free...
}
}


lzss roundtrip:


c


static void tc_lzss_roundtrip(sdk_test_ctx *t) {
for (int i=0;i<100;i++){
size_t n = 1 + (i*53)%500;
uint8_t *src=malloc(n);
// pattern: random or repeated
for j: if i%3==0 src[j]=0; else if i%3==1 src[j]=(j%7); else src[j]=random
size_t cap = n*2+64; uint8_t *comp=malloc(cap); size_t clen;
SDK_T_EQ_ST(t, sdk_lzss_compress(src,n,comp,cap,&clen), SDK_OK);
uint8_t *dec=malloc(n+16); size_t dlen;
SDK_T_EQ_ST(t, sdk_lzss_decompress(comp,clen,dec,n+16,&dlen), SDK_OK);
SDK_T_EQ_MEM(t, src, dec, n);
}
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
VS="$ROOT"  # not used
VC="/c/Program Files (x86)/Microsoft Visual Studio/2022/BuildTools/VC/Tools/MSVC/14.41.34120"
SDK="/c/Program Files (x86)/Windows Kits/10"
SDKVER="10.0.22621.0"
export PATH="$VC/bin/Hostx64/x64:$PATH"
export INCLUDE="$VC/include;$SDK/Include/$SDKVER/um;$SDK/Include/$SDKVER/shared;$SDK/Include/$SDKVER/winrt;$SDK/Include/$SDKVER/ucrt"
export LIB="$VC/lib/x64;$SDK/Lib/$SDKVER/um/x64;$SDK/Lib/$SDKVER/ucrt/x64"
NAME="$1"; shift
OBJ="$ROOT/build/obj/$NAME"; BIN="$ROOT/build/bin"; LOG="$ROOT/build/logs"
mkdir -p "$OBJ" "$BIN" "$LOG"
rm -f "$OBJ"/*.obj
CFLAGS="/nologo /std:c17 /W4 /WX /O2 /Zi /MT /GS /Gy /utf-8 /DUNICODE /D_UNICODE /DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN /D_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS /I\"$ROOT/include\""
LDFLAGS="/nologo /DEBUG /INCREMENTAL:NO /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF /DYNAMICBASE /NXCOMPAT /HIGHENTROPYVA /MACHINE:X64"
LDLIBS="kernel32.lib user32.lib gdi32.lib bcrypt.lib"
echo "=== compile $NAME ===" > "$LOG/$NAME.log"
cl $CFLAGS /c /Fo"$OBJ\\" /Fd"$OBJ\\$NAME.pdb" "$@" >> "$LOG/$NAME.log" 2>&1
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo "CC_FAIL"; cat "$LOG/$NAME.log"; exit 1; fi
echo "=== link $NAME ===" >> "$LOG/$NAME.log"
link $LDFLAGS /SUBSYSTEM:CONSOLE /OUT:"$BIN\\$NAME.exe" /PDB:"$BIN\\$NAME.pdb" "$OBJ\\*.obj" $LDLIBS >> "$LOG/$NAME.log" 2>&1
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo "LINK_FAIL"; cat "$LOG/$NAME.log"; exit 1; fi
echo "EXITCODE=0" >> "$LOG/$NAME.log"
echo "ok: $BIN/$NAME.exe"

static sdk_status tv_write_blob_for_entry(tv_repo *r, const tv_index_entry *e) {
wchar_t *wpath = NULL;

uint8_t *data = NULL; size_t len = 0; uint32_t we = 0;

tv_oid id;

st = tv_write_object(r, TV_OBJ_BLOB, data, len, id);
free(data);
return st;
}

c


static sdk_status write_blob_for_entry(tv_repo *r, const tv_index_entry *e) {
wchar_t *wpath = NULL;
if (root_path(r, e->path, &wpath) != SDK_OK) return SDK_ERR_NOMEM;
uint8_t *data=NULL; size_t len=0; uint32_t we=0;
sdk_status st = sdk_file_read_all_w(wpath, SDK_LIMIT_FILE_BYTES, &data, &len, &we);
free(wpath);
if (st != SDK_OK) return st;
tv_oid id; tv_object_id_for("blob", data, len, id);
int ex=0;
if (tv_object_exists(r, id, &ex)==SDK_OK && ex) { free(data); return SDK_OK; }
st = tv_write_object(r, TV_OBJ_BLOB, data, len, id);
free(data);
return st;
}


But root_path is static in tinyvcs_core.c — not accessible from test. I'll compute the path manually: tv_join(r->root, sdk_utf8_to_utf16(e->path,...)). r->root and r->meta are public. So I can build the work path directly. Good — avoids needing root_path.


Let me write do_commit:


c


static sdk_status do_commit(tv_repo *r, const char *author, const char *msg,
const char *const *paths, const char *const *contents,
size_t n) {
tv_index idx; tv_index_init(&idx);
tv_oid *blobs = malloc(n*sizeof(tv_oid));
uint8_t *flags = malloc(n);
for (size_t i=0;i<n;i++){
// write file
wchar_t *wp = tv_join(r->root, sdk_utf8_to_utf16(paths[i], strlen(paths[i]), NULL));
sdk_file_write_all_w(wp, contents[i], strlen(contents[i]), NULL);
free(wp);
// blob id
tv_oid id;
wchar_t *wp2 = tv_join(r->root, sdk_utf8_to_utf16(paths[i], strlen(paths[i]), NULL));
tv_file_blob_id(wp2, id, NULL, NULL);
free(wp2);
// write blob object
uint8_t *data; size_t len; uint32_t we;
sdk_file_read_all_w(compute path...);
tv_object_id_for("blob", data,len,id);
int ex; if(!tv_object_exists(r,id,&ex)&&!ex) tv_write_object(r,TV_OBJ_BLOB,data,len,id);
free(data);
// index entry
tv_index_entry e; memset(&e,0,sizeof e);
snprintf(e.path,...,"%s",paths[i]); e.stage_state=0;
memcpy(e.blob, id, 32); e.size=len;
tv_index_upsert(&idx,&e);
memcpy(blobs[i], id, 32); flags[i]=0;
}
tv_oid root_tree;
tv_build_tree_from_paths(r, paths, blobs, flags, n, &root_tree);
char branch[...]; tv_head_branch(r, branch, sizeof branch);
tv_oid parent; int unborn;
tv_read_ref(r, branch, &parent, &unborn);
tv_oid commit_id;
tv_create_commit(r, unborn?NULL:&parent, &root_tree, author, msg, commit_id);
tv_write_ref(r, branch, &commit_id);
tv_index_save(r, &idx);
free(blobs); free(flags); tv_index_free(&idx);
return SDK_OK;
}

static void test_status_classification(sdk_test_ctx *t) {

For the solve loop:


c


static int solve_all(sdk_app *a) {
for (int i = 0; i < SDK_BOARD_CELLS; ++i) {
if (a->given_mask[i]) continue;
a->selected = i;
sdk_app_place_digit(a, a->solution.cells[i].value);
}
return a->state == SDK_APP_COMPLETED;
}


Test lifecycle:


c


static void ti_lifecycle(sdk_test_ctx *t) {
sdk_app *a = sdk_app_create(960, 720, NULL, NULL, 0);
SDK_T_TRUE(t, a != NULL);
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, (int)SDK_APP_MENU, (int)a->state);
sdk_app_new_game(a, SDK_DIFF_EASY);
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, (int)SDK_APP_PLAYING, (int)a->state);
int clues = 0;
for (int i=0;i<SDK_BOARD_CELLS;++i) clues += a->given_mask[i];
SDK_T_TRUE(t, clues >= 17 && clues <= 60);
SDK_T_TRUE(t, solve_all(a));
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, (int)SDK_APP_COMPLETED, (int)a->state);
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, 0, a->mistakes);
sdk_app_to_menu(a);
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, (int)SDK_APP_MENU, (int)a->state);
sdk_app_destroy(a);
}


Note: SDK_T_EQ_I compares ints. State is enum; cast to int.

static void te_keyboard_play(sdk_test_ctx *t) {
sdk_app *a = sdk_app_create(960,720,NULL,NULL,0);

if(a->given_mask[i]) continue;
a->selected=i;

}

sdk_app_on_key(a, 0x0D, 0); // Enter on completed -> new game
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, (int)SDK_APP_PLAYING, (int)a->state);
sdk_app_destroy(a);
}

static void te_mistake(sdk_test_ctx *t) {

SDK_T_EQ_I(t, (int)SDK_APP_PLAYING, (int)a->state);
// correct it
sdk_app_on_key(a, 0x08, 0); // backspace clears
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, 0, (int)a->current.cells[c].value);
// solve rest
solve_all(a);
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, (int)SDK_APP_COMPLETED, (int)a->state);
SDK_T_EQ_I(t, 1, a->mistakes);
sdk_app_destroy(a);
}

Now I see the bug clearly. At line 2476-2482, the tree is built only from stage_state == 0 entries (present). Good. But at line 2484-2489, the loop iterates for (size_t i = 0; i < pi; ++i) where pi is the number of PRESENT entries, but it indexes idx.entries[i] — which is WRONG!
